tools.name: x402
tools.description: HTTP-native fixed-price settlement for machine requests. A client receives 402 terms, pays in USDC through a facilitator, then retries with proof.
tools.caveat: Settlement, not trust; not built for streaming payments.

tools.name: Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
tools.description: A mandate layer for proving that a human authorized an agent purchase envelope, using signed intent, cart and payment artifacts.
tools.caveat: AP2 authorizes; it does not move money.

tools.name: Machine Payments Protocol (MPP)
tools.description: Stripe and Tempo’s machine-to-machine settlement model, with charge and session intents and backward compatibility with x402.
tools.caveat: New in 2026; adoption and demand remain unproven.

tools.name: AgentCore Payments
tools.description: AWS preview combining a managed wallet, session limits and payment audit for AWS agents, with Coinbase CDP or Stripe Privy integrations.
tools.caveat: Platform-locked and described as preview in the research.

tools.name: Pinout
tools.description: An implementation reference exploring the gap between one-shot x402 charges and metered or session-style billing.
tools.caveat: The research characterizes this class as demos, not proven demand.

tools.name: ERC-8004
tools.description: On-chain identity, reputation and validation registries for agents. The standard deliberately leaves score calculation to outside systems.
tools.caveat: Raw feedback can be Sybil-vulnerable; a registry is not a trust score.

tools.name: Vouch
tools.description: A build-in-public trust layer producing payer and payee scores plus ALLOW, WARN or BLOCK decisions for x402 interactions.
tools.caveat: No dominant paid traction was found.

tools.name: AgentCredit
tools.description: An experimental reputation-priced x402 project using zero-knowledge proofs on Base Sepolia.
tools.caveat: Experimental; not evidence of a mature paid market.

tools.name: SpendVeto
tools.description: Deterministic spend controls with caps, budgets, approvals, kill switch, idempotency replay, dry-run and time-boxed grants.
tools.caveat: The research found no evidence of paid customers.

tools.name: Virtuals Programmable Wallets
tools.description: Server-side wallet policy controls for agents, including restrictive presets such as DENY_ALL and ACP_ONLY.
tools.caveat: Wallet-specific rather than a neutral cross-rail control plane.

tools.name: MCP Registry / Harbor
tools.description: Indexes MCP servers so builders can discover remote tools. The research cites roughly 9,652 servers in the official registry and 31,486 indexed by Harbor in 2026.
tools.caveat: Listing scale is not live-delivery verification.

tools.name: Agent2Agent (A2A)
tools.description: A delegation protocol using Agent Cards and a task lifecycle for agents that need to coordinate across organizations.
tools.caveat: Different layer from MCP tool calling; negotiation volume remains small.

tools.name: FetchGate Bazaar Audit
tools.description: A public crawl and audit of x402 Bazaar listings, focused on availability, price, payer counts and listing churn.
tools.caveat: A dated crawl; it does not prove a paid endpoint currently delivers.

tools.name: Mem0
tools.description: A prominent long-term memory layer for agents, with a hosted API and integration into the broader agent ecosystem.
tools.caveat: A crowded, well-funded category rather than an empty market.

tools.name: Zep / Graphiti
tools.description: Temporal knowledge-graph memory for agents, aimed at retaining and retrieving changing context over time.
tools.caveat: Compared here from secondary research; check current product docs before use.

tools.name: Letta
tools.description: An OS-inspired agent memory approach with layered memory and git-backed context repositories described in the 2026 research.
tools.caveat: Memory infrastructure is already competitive and hyperscaler-bundled.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.description: Open-source tracing and evaluation infrastructure in the crowded agent observability category.
tools.caveat: Generic observability is a mature, crowded market.

tools.name: Braintrust
tools.description: Evaluation-driven tooling for testing and monitoring AI systems, included in the research’s observability comparison set.
tools.caveat: Check current limits and pricing directly; no live verification was performed.

tools.name: Daytona
tools.description: Managed execution infrastructure for running agent-generated code in isolated environments.
tools.caveat: Capital-intensive and crowded; pricing in the report came from secondary comparisons.

tools.name: E2B
tools.description: Cloud sandboxes designed for AI-generated code and computer-use workloads.
tools.caveat: Use the comparison as orientation, then verify current product details directly.

tools.name: Manifest by Manifold
tools.description: MCP security scoring and asset inventory; the cited research reported 7,700 servers scored and 206,000 assets indexed.
tools.caveat: Enterprise agent security is a crowded, funded market.

tools.name: Arcade
tools.description: Agent tool authorization infrastructure included in the research’s funded enterprise security set.
tools.caveat: Enterprise-focused; read the vendor profile and current docs before adopting.

tools.name: Aembit
tools.description: Access-control infrastructure extending workload identity concepts to personal AI agents.
tools.caveat: Identity is crowded and frequently bundled by enterprise platforms.

tools.name: Okta for AI Agents
tools.description: Enterprise identity and governance controls for agents inside Okta’s broader identity control plane.
tools.caveat: The cited 2026 analysis says pricing and product details remained unresolved.
